beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW - hesitant writer BLUF. Misconception corrected: 'rebuilt this game from scratch' -> 'extended one existing slice', the reel's actual scope claim (see README.md 'Known limitations').
beats.narration_text: Walker extended one existing slice - it didn't rebuild the game. One new character, Crate-Bot. One new zone, three jumps deeper. The collider, the movement tuning, the retry loop: all untouched. The one genuinely new thing is a real decision - how you take the second jump decides whether you clear a spike or need a second try.

beats.narration_text: This is walker-jumpman's First Steps slice: cross two gaps, clear a spike patch, reach the flag. One jump, no double jump, unlimited retries. Yuan Jingya's build - with Claude Code - keeps every one of those rules exactly as the starter shipped them, and adds to them instead of replacing them.

Same eighteen-by-twenty-eight collider, same jump height, same acceleration curve as the starter's character. Zone one and Zone two play exactly as they always did.

beats.role_note: ILLUSTRATE LAW - real source diff (git show 2569dc4), not a reconstruction. Sets up the cause-and-effect beat: bug description here -> fixed behavior on screen in B07.
beats.narration_text: A human playtest caught a real defect here. The sign explaining the Zone-three decision was drawn at the zone's entrance - the takeoff for the first gap - not at the ledge where the decision actually happens. By the time the player needed it, it had scrolled off screen behind them. The fix, commit two-five-six-nine-d-c-four: move two lines forty pixels right and thirteen pixels up, onto the ledge itself, above the jump arc so the character never covers them.

beats.narration_text: The alternate route: never stop. Carry full running speed off the ledge, and one continuous jump clears the gap and the spike patch in a single arc. Same tuning, same jump height - just different timing. The fast line and the cautious line both work. Neither is a hard gate.

beats.role_note: Real Godot capture, scripted-input. Zone-3-specific genuine failure - shows the cautious route is a real skill check, not automatically safe.
beats.narration_text: The cautious route can still go wrong. Stop on the ledge, then hop too soon - before enough of a run-up - and the jump comes up short, straight into the gap. Real physics, a real death, the same respawn as anywhere else in the level. Caution only pays off if the second jump is actually timed.

beats.role_note: ClaudeVerdictArtifact. Separates observed-working from open items, per SKILL.md walker-mode Verdict requirement.
beats.narration_text: Verdict. The automated suite is clean: twenty-five of twenty-five mechanics checks, nine of nine keyboard checks, the original two zones provably untouched. Two real defects were found and fixed by inspection and by playtesting, not assumed away - an invisible visor pupil, and the Zone-three sign you just saw fixed. What's still open: only one playtester has run this build, and a dash-pickup idea was deliberately scoped out rather than bolted on.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW. Prompt targets exactly the defect class B06/B07 demonstrated - legibility from the actual decision point, not just 'visible somewhere on screen'.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: 'I added a new zone to my Godot platformer with two required jumps and a hazard. Read my draw calls and tell me: is the hint text actually visible from the exact position the player stands in when the decision has to be made - not just visible somewhere on screen?' That question is exactly the one a real human playtest caught here. Run it on your own level before you ship it. Liam, in for Bear.
